prompt: Normalize the raw REPL input into `cmd`: no surrounding whitespace or newline, lowercase.
why: strip() with no args removes spaces, tabs and newlines from both ends.

prompt: Build `out`: the uppercase first letter of each word followed by a dot. Runs of spaces must not produce empty words.
why: split() with NO argument collapses whitespace runs and drops empties; split(' ') does not.

prompt: Set `city` to `raw` with whitespace collapsed to single spaces and each word capitalized.
why: capitalize() also lowercases the rest of the word, so YORK becomes York.

prompt: Split `line` into `cmd`, `model`, `prompt`. The prompt keeps its inner spacing exactly; ignore leading whitespace. (All three parts are present here.)
given: line = '  run phi3:mini tell me  a joke'
check: assert (cmd, model, prompt) == ('run', 'phi3:mini', 'tell me  a joke')
why: maxsplit=2 stops after two splits so the rest stays verbatim; lstrip first or the first part is ''.

prompt: Shell-style split `line` into `tokens` (quoted text stays one token). If the quotes are unbalanced, `tokens` must be None instead of crashing.
check:
assert tokens is None, tokens
rerun(line='add "New York" --unit C')
assert tokens == ['add', 'New York', '--unit', 'C'], tokens
why: shlex.split raises ValueError ('No closing quotation') on unbalanced quotes.

prompt: Format `row` with one f-string: name left-aligned in 12, size right-aligned in 5 with 1 decimal, then ' GB'.
why: Format spec is align, width, .precision, type: {x:>5.1f}.

prompt: Set `ok` to True if `text` is a palindrome, ignoring case and anything that isn't a letter or digit.
given: text = 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama!'
answer:
chars = [c.casefold() for c in text if c.isalnum()]
ok = chars == chars[::-1]
why: Filter with isalnum(), compare to its [::-1] reverse.

prompt: Run-length encode `s` into `out` using itertools.groupby. Single characters get no count.
answer:
out = ""
for ch, grp in groupby(s):
    n = len(list(grp))
    out += ch if n == 1 else f"{ch}{n}"
why: groupby yields (key, iterator) for each run of equal items; len(list(grp)) counts the run.

prompt: Walk `args` with an index: every '--name' consumes the NEXT arg as its value into `flags`; every other arg goes into `words`.
why: A while loop with a manual index can skip ahead by 2; a for loop can't.

prompt: Greedy word wrap: append each word to `current` if it still fits within `width` (single spaces), otherwise push `current` onto `lines` and start over. Flush at the end.
given:
text, width = 'the quick brown fox jumps', 10
lines, current = [], ''
why: The +1 is the joining space; remember the final flush after the loop.

prompt: Replace each {{ key }} in `tpl` (any inner whitespace) with str(ctx[key]); leave unknown keys exactly as written. Use re.sub with a function. Result in `out`.
answer: out = re.sub(r"\{\{\s*(\w+)\s*\}\}", lambda m: str(ctx[m.group(1)]) if m.group(1) in ctx else m.group(0), tpl)
check: assert out == 'Hi Jack, 3 new, {{ x }}', out
why: re.sub accepts a function of the Match; group(0) is the whole match, group(1) the capture.

prompt: Parse `line` with re.fullmatch and named groups date, time, level (DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR), source (inside [...]) and message. Set `d` to the groupdict, or None if it doesn't match.
given:
import re
line = '2026-09-14 10:03:22 ERROR [provider] Model not loaded: phi3'
answer:
m = re.fullmatch(r"(?P<date>\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (?P<time>\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}) (?P<level>DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR) \[(?P<source>[^\]]+)\] (?P<message>.*)", line)
d = m.groupdict() if m else None
check: assert d == {'date': '2026-09-14', 'time': '10:03:22', 'level': 'ERROR', 'source': 'provider', 'message': 'Model not loaded: phi3'}, d
why: (?P<name>...) names a group; groupdict() returns them all. fullmatch anchors both ends.
